title: Noah and the Great Ark
summary: Noah builds a huge ark, and his neighbors laugh at him, but he keeps building day after day. The animals come in two by two and learn to live together in the warm ark while a great rain falls outside. A story about not giving up, caring for every creature, and the rainbow, God's promise.
pages:
Once, many, many years ago, there lived a good man named Noah.
He had a long white beard and a wooden hammer in his hand.
Knock, knock, knock — Noah was building something big.

"What are you building?" asked the neighbors.
"An ark," answered Noah. "God told me a great rain is coming."
The neighbors laughed: "Rain? An ark? What nonsense!"

Noah didn't get angry. He just kept on building.
Beam after beam, nail after nail.
Year after year, until the ark was as tall as a mountain.

And then the animals came.
Two elephants — boom, boom.
Two rabbits — hop, hop.
Two giraffes bent down to fit through the door.

Lions too, and ants, and frogs, and parrots.
Two by two, they all went into the ark.
Noah and his family went in last, and God closed the door.

Drip, drip, drip... and then shhhhh!
Outside, the rain came pouring down hard.
But inside the ark it was dry and warm and cozy.

There was lots of work in the ark.
Noah fed all the animals, each one at its own time.
Hay for the cows, seeds for the birds, and a big meal for the lion.

The animals learned to live together.
The cat didn't chase the mouse, and the mouse wasn't afraid of the cat.
At night everyone fell asleep to the sound of the rain: pitter, patter, pit.

One day the rain stopped.
Noah opened a little window and sent out a white dove.
"Go and see if there is dry land yet," he asked.

In the evening the dove came back, and in her beak was a green olive leaf!
"There are trees!" Noah cried happily.
All the animals jumped and danced in the ark.

When the land was dry, everyone went outside.
The elephants stomped, the rabbits hopped, and the birds flew up high.
And the sun warmed them all.

Then a rainbow of every color appeared in the sky.
"This is My sign," said God.
"A promise that there will never again be a flood over the world."

Even today, after the rain, you can sometimes see a rainbow.
And when you see one, you can remember Noah,
who kept on building, and cared for every animal, big and small.
